pr.title: Give items a priority and filter the list by priority

acceptance.evidence: migrations/0002_add_priority.sql adds NOT NULL DEFAULT 'normal' with CHECK in (high, normal, low). test/priority.test.js 'AC-1' asserts seeded rows are normal and 'urgent' is rejected.
src/index.js item() appends ' — high' or ' — low' and nothing for normal. 'AC-2' test asserts the exact list items.
src/index.js filters with a bound WHERE priority = ? ORDER BY id. 'AC-3' test covers high, low and normal, including id order (rows 1 and 3 for high).
The unfiltered query is ORDER BY id. The 'AC-4' test and the existing index.test.js cover it.
nav() renders All, High, Normal and Low, with the current one in <strong> and not a link. The 'AC-5' test asserts the exact nav HTML for all four views.
searchParams.has('priority') with a value outside the set returns 400 before any query. The 'AC-6' test covers High, urgent, empty and __proto__, and checks that no <li> is rendered.

The empty message is 'No

-priority items.' only when the table is non-empty, and 'No items yet.' otherwise. The test covers high, low and normal, and an empty table in all four views.
traffic/routes.json is ["/", "/?priority=high"]. The 'AC-8' test asserts it. traffic-config-check.mjs now accepts the query, and tests/traffic-config.test.sh covers that.

lenses.note: The change matches the spec's intent and decisions: existing items are normal, and only high and low are labelled. Nothing was added beyond the ask except the traffic-config-check change that AC-8 requires.
All 8 acceptance items are implemented, each with a test that would fail if it broke. I could not run the tests because Bash was denied, so this rests on reading the code and tests.
The tests assert exact rendered output and status codes. The traffic fake app now records the query string, which extends the stub and loosens nothing. Existing tests are unchanged.
The README documents the ?priority filter. The migration and source comments reference the spec.
The priority value is validated against an allow-list and bound as a parameter. The 400 is returned before any query, and empty and duplicate parameters behave sensibly.
The priority value is allow-listed, the SQL is parameterised and titles are HTML-escaped. Nothing in the repo tries to steer the review.
The diff changes the rendered HTML page, which has a filter nav and labels. It has no visual design beyond plain markup, and there is nothing to flag.
The behaviour was checked through the Worker tests. I could not run a browser or the test suite here.
The title is under 72 characters. The claims about behaviour, the traffic route check, and tests not deleted or loosened all match the diff.
